diagnoses.summary: PCA detects a high SPE with coherent T2 movement dominated by H2 vent and reactor pressure signals, pointing to an H2 PCV-related fault propagating through the system. The strongest evidence is the H2 PCV/vent-related faults with PCV-stuck behavior and pressure effects.

PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with reactor pressure rising and H2 vent control under abnormal conditions. Alarms indicate reactor pressure high/high-high. Most consistent with H2 PCV fault causing pressure buildup.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with reactor pressure rising and H2 vent flow contributing strongly. Alarm flags confirm high reactor pressure. Likely H2 PCV issue causing insufficient venting, with possible sensor bias and PCV degradation contributing.

The PCA shows a large, coherent plant upset with strong evidence pointing to the hydrogen vent (H2 PCV) pathway being abnormal, causing elevated reactor pressure and vented flow signals. The top contributors indicate the CSTR pressure spike and H2 vent flow changes are driving the abnormality, with high alarms on reactor pressure.
Abnormal PCA with large, coherent move along normal correlations and large SPE, dominated by reactor pressure and H2 vent variables; likely H2 PCV fault causing reactor pressure rise.

Abnormal PCA with large, coherent disturbance in both T2 and SPE, dominated by reactor pressure variables and H2 vent signals. Evidence points to H2 PCV (vent valve) issue causing reactor pressure rise and compensatory control actions.
Abnormal PCA with large coherent upset dominated by reactor pressure/vent behavior. Strong evidence for H2 PCV-related fault causing elevated CSTR pressure and high VOC vent response.

PCA abnormal with both T2 and SPE violations; strongest evidence points to the hydrogen vent (PCV) path being blocked or degraded, causing elevated reactor pressure and compensatory signals downstream.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with a strong reactor pressure rise driven by H2 purge system issues. Alarms on reactor pressure (R_P_H, R_P_HH) corroborate a high-pressure condition likely caused by the H2 PCV path not opening as required, i.e., PCV-related fault.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with reactor pressure driving the disturbance; multiple fault hypotheses point to the hydrogen PCV (H2 PCV) path, with PCV-related faults and a pressure sensor bias as secondary possibilities.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations. The strongest contributor is reactor pressure-related signals, pointing to issues with the H2 PCV subsystem and related pressure sensing/valving rather than a random sensor fault.
PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with reactor pressure and PCV-related signals driving the abnormality. Likely H2 PCV fault combined with a secondary condenser/pressure issue.

A large, coherent process upset with both T2 and SPE violated. Key contributors are the R_PIC and RB_LIC control outputs and measured CSTR pressure, with a distal disturbance from the distillate/acetone purity alarm. Likely root causes point to saturated/out-of-range controllers and possible H2 PCV issues or condenser performance degradation.

The abnormal PCA when both T2 and SPE are violated (high T2 and high SPE) with dominant contribution from reactor pressure-related signals and evidence of PCV-related anomalies strongly points to an H2 PCV (cstr_vent_valve) fault causing a coherent process upset.

PCA shows a large, coherent process upset with strong reactor pressure-related signals and a saturated reflux control loop. Most likely a fault in the H2 PCV path causing abnormal reactor pressure control and downstream feed adjustments.

PCA flags a large, coherent process upset with simultaneous high T² and high SPE, dominated by CSTR pressure signal and a saturated PID loop on R_PIC. The evidence points to a malfunction in the hydrogen vent (PCV) path causing pressure control trouble and subsequent reactor/system responses.
Abnormal PCA with large coherent upset centered on reactor pressure; likely H2 PCV fault causing high reactor pressure and loop compensation running toward limit.

PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with both T² and SPE violations. Most evidence points to a H2 PCV (cstr_vent_valve) related fault driving reactor pressure up, with PCV behavior degraded or stuck. The dominant contribution is to reactor pressure measurement (meas.cstr_pressure_bar) and PCV command/actuation (op.R_PIC).

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violated. The dominant contributor is reactor pressure (cstr_pressure_bar) with strong load on the H2 PCV control loop (R_PIC is saturated). This points to a fault in the H2 PCV valve and its actuator/signal path, most likely degradation or a sticking condition, causing high reactor pressure and compensatory action at the PCV controller.

The PCA shows a large, coherent plant upset with simultaneous T^2 and SPE violations. The strongest evidence points to a fault related to the H2 PCV (cstr_vent_valve) acting abnormally, likely limiting reactor pressure relief and driving a high-pressure response in the CSTR.
Severe, coherent plant upset with strong evidence pointing to H2 PCV (vent) related faults causing reactor pressure anomalies and saturated control loops.
Abnormal PCA with large coherent upset dominated by reactor pressure and PCV/controller interaction; likely H2 PCV fault causing high reactor pressure and saturated R_PIC loop.

The PCA shows a large, coherent plant upset with both Hotelling T² and SPE violated. The strongest evidence points to a fault in the hydrogen purge (H2 PCV) path, with the PCV actuator (cstr_vent_valve) likely degraded or stuck, causing reactor pressure to drift high and the PCV to misbehave. A sensor bias on the reactor pressure could also contribute, but the ruling highlights PCV-related actuator faults as the primary cause.

PCA shows a large, coherent plant upset with reactor pressure related measurements dominating the disturbance; the R_PIC loop is saturated and its output is at its limit while the PV is far from the setpoint. Fault hypotheses point to H2 PCV issues driving the upset, with R_PIC out-of-range behavior also plausible.
Abnormal PCA with high T² and high SPE dominated by CSTR pressure signal; PCV-related issue likely causing reactor pressure rise and loop compensation saturation.

PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with strong evidence pointing to H2 PCV (cstr_vent_valve) issues causing elevated reactor pressure; multiple fault hypotheses relate to the H2 PCV performance. R_PIC saturation and pressure indications support PCV-related faults as primary cause.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations, dominated by the CSTR pressure measurement and PCV-related signals, plus a saturated PIC loop. Sensor bias and PCV-related faults are implicated, with possible accompanying process faults toward CSTR outlet flow/level. Most likely a PCV-related issue causing abnormal reactor pressure readings and loop compensation, with secondary evidence of a pressure sensor bias and outlet capacity effects.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset centered on the CSTR pressure with strong contribution from the H2 PCV control loop. The evidence points to a fault in the H2 PCV (vent valve) capability or position, causing reactor pressure to rise and the PCV command/actual behavior to mismatch, with R_PIC saturating and compensating loops driven to extreme setpoints.

PCA detects a large, coherent process upset with strong evidence pointing at the hydrogen vent (PCV) / reactor pressure control path. The most likely root cause is an H2 PCV fault causing reactor pressure rise, with possible sensor bias contributing to the SPE.

PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with strong reactor pressure-related effects and loop saturation indicative of H2 PCV (vent) issues propagating through the process. Likely PCV fault(s) causing pressure control problems.

PCA indicates a large, coherent plant upset with strong contribution from reactor pressure measurement and loop actions saturating. The most consistent fault is an H2 PCV related actuator issue causing reactor pressure rise and compensatory saturation in PIC/LIC loops; sensor bias also plausible given the dominant pressure measurement in SPE.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong reactor pressure involvement and saturated control loops around the hydrogen PCV and related feed/outlet controls, consistent with H2 PCV impairment plus related upstream/downstream flow control saturation and a possible condenser issue.

Abnormal PCA: large, coherent process upset with both T² and SPE violations, and multiple controller loops saturated. Likely H2 PCV (cstr vent valve) fault causing reactor pressure upset and cascading loop actions.

PCA flags a coherent process upset with strong reactor-side pressure contribution and saturated control loops; sensor correlations largely preserved but several loops are saturated and an H2 vent valve issue is suspected.
